toxicity_note: Can be toxic to dogs, cats and horses if eaten in quantity.
Seeds and roots are toxic if eaten.
All parts are toxic if eaten, and the sap can irritate skin and eyes. Toxic to pets and livestock.
Can cause skin irritation in some people. It is a relative of poison ivy, though a much milder one.
Berries are mildly toxic if eaten in quantity.
Leaves, stems and pits are poisonous if eaten, and toxic to pets and livestock. Fruit is safe only when cooked and pitted.
Raw berries, leaves, stems and roots can cause stomach upset. Cook berries before eating.
Acorns and young leaves are toxic to livestock and can harm dogs if eaten in quantity.
